title: Kernel Determinism Investigation and Replay Protocol
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This playbook documents a structured protocol for investigating non-deterministic latency or correctness regressions that appear to originate from kernel execution or kernel-selection behavior in the serving runtime. It provides a hypothesis-driven replay workflow, the required data artifacts, checklist of signals to inspect, and a reproducible sandbox procedure for iterating on kernel-level fixes. The intent is to reduce mean time to root cause for kernels that produce intermittent slow paths or divergent outputs across retries.

Scope

- Applies to runtime versions 2023.11 and later and to kernels managed by the kernel mapper (kmux).
- Focuses on issues where the same request input produces different execution characteristics (latency, kernel choice, memory usage) across retries or across replicas.
- Excludes: pure network/transit issues (see eng-sre incident runbooks), and model-level randomness that is expected by design (e.g., sampling).

Definitions

- Determinism failure: the same complete request (headers, model version, prompt, session KV state) produces different kernel selection, resource consumption, or tail latency without legitimate reason.
- Replay corpus: a saved set of requests + runtime context used to deterministically re-run workload in a sandbox.
- Kernel trace: annotated timeline of kernel lifecycle events (select, load, handshake, exec_begin, exec_end, evict).

When to use this playbook

- Tail latency spikes that correlate with kernel-change events in traces (kernel_swap, kernel_fallback).
- Flaky regression test failures in the throughput bench that cannot be reproduced by simple load replay.
- Divergent telemetry across cold and warm runs where KV cache and kernel-choice paths differ.

Prerequisites and permissions

- Access to the runtime profiling cluster and ability to create sandbox sandboxes (incubation clusters) — request via infra-ticket-jenkins with tag "profiling-sandbox".
- Read access to kernel binary registry and kernel metadata (kmux/catalog service).
- Tools: local replay harness (repo: infra/replay-harness), trace-analyzer (repo: infra/trace-tools), a copy of the production request-sampler export (stored in /artifacts/profiles/year-month).

High-level workflow (quick view)

1) Triage: capture representative requests and runtime traces.
2) Isolate: build a minimal replay corpus that reproduces divergence.
3) Replay: run deterministic replay under the sandbox with full kernel telemetry enabled.
4) Hypothesize: enumerate kernel-level causes and validate by controlled experiments.
5) Patch & validate: deploy kernel fix to canary and run regression suite.

Detailed procedure

1) Triage and initial capture

- Collect the request payloads and full trace IDs for 10-100 affected requests. Include: request headers, model name+commit, session_id, router route, and exact timestamp. Example required metadata JSON (single-line):

  {"request_id":"<id>","model":"redwood-open-7b-v2","seq_len":128,"route":"text.generate","trace_id":"abcd-1234"}

- Pull the trace events using trace-analyzer:

  trace-analyzer export --trace-id abcd-1234 --out /tmp/trace-abcd.json

- Identify kernel events: search for event types select_kernel, kernel_load, kernel_exec_begin, kernel_exec_end, kernel_evict. Record kernel binary hash, node id, and slot_id.

2) Build a deterministic replay corpus

- For each request record: full body, headers, KV cache snapshot (if available), and the exact model variant string (e.g., redwood-open-7b-v2@2025-11-03-rc2).
- Prefer requests that: previously triggered both fast and slow outcomes; have identical inputs; and show kernel-choice flip in traces.
- Store corpus under: /artifacts/replay-corpora/kernel-determinism/<run-id>/corpus.jsonl . Each line is a JSON object with flat fields.

3) Configure sandbox for deterministic replay

- Provision a sandbox cluster with identical software ABI and kernel catalog. Use the infra playbook to pin: runtime image (sha256), kmux catalog revision, and kernel binaries revision.
- Enable deterministic runtime flags in /etc/runtime/conf.d/replay.toml:

  [replay]
  enforce_kv_snapshot = true
  disable_dynamic_kernel_prefetch = true
  seed_kernel_mapper = "fixed"

- Start the sandbox runtime with kernel telemetry level = 5 and trace sampling = 100%.

4) Run replay and capture outputs

- Command (example):

  replay-harness run --corpus /artifacts/replay-corpora/kernel-determinism/<run-id>/corpus.jsonl --target http://sandbox-runtime:8080 --concurrency 4 --repeat 3 --write-traces /tmp/replay-traces

- For each replay iteration, collect: latency percentile distribution, kernel trace files, kernel binary checksums, and any divergence in model output tokens.

5) Hypothesis generation and controlled experiments

- Common hypothesis patterns to test: 
  - Kernel handshake race: two concurrent requests caused a different kernel to be selected due to a timing window.
  - Eviction-induced cold path: aggressive eviction policy allowed a kernel to be reloaded on hot path causing startup overhead.
  - Kernel compatibility fallback: kmux selected a binary variant with different quantization profile under memory pressure.
  - Kernel threading/SM occupancy variance: same kernel executed at different GPU occupancy causing execution time variability.

- For each hypothesis, design a minimal controlled change and re-run the replay:
  1. Handshake race: serialize kernel selection with a 10ms mutex and observe if flip disappears.
  2. Eviction: increase kernel hot-cache TTL to 300s during replay.
  3. Compatibility fallback: pin kernel selection to the primary binary (force_kmux_binary = <hash>).
  4. Occupancy: pin GPU affinity to single SM mask to measure per-kernel exec time variance.

6) Observability signals and acceptance thresholds

- Signals to inspect (table described in text):
  - metric: kernel_select_rate_change -> acceptable: <= 2x baseline during repro
  - metric: exec_time_p95 (per-kernel) -> acceptable: p95 within 10% of baseline for stable kernels
  - event: kernel_fallback_count -> acceptable: 0 for deterministic-corpus runs
  - log: handshake_timeout -> acceptable: none

- If any signal exceeds the threshold, mark the hypothesis as plausible and escalate to kernel-owner.

7) Patch, canary, and regression suite

- If a kernel binary or kernel-selection policy change is required:
  - Build a kernel binary with debug symbols and a short-lived toggle flag.
  - Canaries: deploy to a single sandbox shard and run the full replay corpus 10x.
  - Regression: add a synthetic test to the microbench that replays the failing corpus and assert median+p95 latency and kernel_fallback_count == 0.

8) Postmortem artefacts and documentation

- Required artifacts for closure: replay corpus, raw traces, diff of kernel catalog, patch PR, canary run logs, and regression test entry. Attach these in the incident ticket and link to this playbook.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: runtime-kernel-team (pager: oncall-kernel).
- Secondary owner: eng-sre (for sandbox provisioning and capacity).
- Escalation path: kernel oncall -> runtime tech lead -> infra reliability director. Use the standard oncall escalation timeline (15/45/90 minutes).

Example artifacts

- Minimal trace extract (abbreviated):
  {
    "trace_id":"abcd-1234",
    "events":[
      {"ts":1678891200123, "type":"select_kernel", "binary":"khash:aa11"},
      {"ts":1678891200150, "type":"kernel_load", "node":"gpu-17"},
      {"ts":1678891200450, "type":"kernel_exec_begin", "slot":3},
      {"ts":1678891200788, "type":"kernel_exec_end", "duration_ms":338}
    ]
  }

- Sample replay harness command for deterministic pinning:
  replay-harness run --pin-binary aa11 --concurrency 1 --repeat 5 --write-traces /tmp/fixed

Runbook checklist (quick reference)

- [ ] Collect 10 representative traces and request payloads.
- [ ] Build deterministic replay corpus and upload to artifacts storage.
- [ ] Provision sandbox with pinned runtime + kernels.
- [ ] Run replay with telemetry = 100% and collect kernel traces.
- [ ] Validate hypothesis with at least one controlled experiment.
- [ ] Patch and run canary + regression tests.
- [ ] Document artifacts and close incident with owners tagged.

Appendix A: Common pitfalls

- Missing KV snapshot: If KV cache snapshot is not available, some nondeterminism will persist. Always prefer requests tied to explicit KV snapshots.
- Environment mismatch: small differences in CUDA/driver versions can produce different SM scheduling behaviour — ensure sandbox matches production drivers at the ABI level.
- Over-interpreting noise: small p50/p75 changes are expected under load; focus on p95/p99 and binary selection flips.

Appendix B: Where to find helpers

- replay-harness: git@github.com:redwood/infra/replay-harness
- trace-analyzer: git@github.com:redwood/infra/trace-tools
- artifacts storage: s3://redwood-internal/profiles/
